summary: Round 6, scoped to the delta since 132bf9c19978: one deleted comment clause in LogKeysTest and three new argued-equivalent entries in baselines/mutants.txt. EVERYTHING WAS RE-MEASURED IN AN ISOLATED TREE (scripts/review-tree.sh test-reviewer), never read. Confirmed green: the restored tree passes ./gradlew test --rerun-tasks, and the repository's staged diff is byte-identical at 9472c5ea19f8. THE SHORTENED COMMENT IS NOW TRUE AND MEASURED: with the `bins.delta` assertion deleted and `startsWith(logPrefix)` narrowed to `startsWith(prefix)`, :sequencer:test is GREEN -- so 'The two cases above miss it' holds, and deleting the false clause was the right call. NO ASSERTION WAS WEAKENED (testing.md rules 4-5): the LogKeysTest hunk is -2/+1 comment lines with zero assertion changes, and every mutant earlier rounds recorded as killed is still killed, re-run individually: round trip -> `return true` (killed by aKeyWhoseDigitsParseButDoNotRegenerate), startsWith guard deleted, endsWith guard deleted, endsWith("delta"), startsWith(prefix) (all four killed by aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammar), plus the four ChainReplay mutants -- chainEnd filter deleted, applyChain filter deleted, chainEnd continue->break, applyChain continue->return -- each killed by ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest. THE THREE NEW MUTANTS.TXT ENTRIES: entries 1 (endsWith->contains) and 2 (reversed equals) are TRUE, and arguing them is the RIGHT call because neither can be killed by any test under a dot-free prefix -- I checked that nothing validates the prefix, only Objects.requireNonNull, so the stated ⚠️ caveat is honest too. ENTRY 3 CARRIES A FALSE MEASUREMENT CLAIM and that is the one blocking finding: the epoch-dropping narrowing it says is 'KILLED by 12 tests' SURVIVES the suite when the operand is derived from logPrefix, the 12 kills come from a hard-coded `bins` literal that most test chains do not use, and the stated mechanism ('a sibling epoch's entries would be read into this chain') is contradicted by all 12 failure messages and is impossible through either call site. The refuted first draft it replaced was the true statement. Remedy is subtractive, or better, one assertion I measured that kills the entire narrowing family and makes entry 3 unnecessary.

findings.file: baselines/mutants.txt:138-148 (third new entry, the two ⚠️ clauses)
findings.title: The 'KILLED by 12 tests' clause is refuted by measurement: the epoch-dropping narrowing SURVIVES, and the 12 kills come from the `prefix` component, not the epoch
findings.detail: The entry's operative claim is TRUE and I reproduced it: `key.startsWith(logPrefix)` narrowed to `logPrefix.substring(0, logPrefix.length() - 1)` leaves :sequencer:test green. Its two ⚠️ clauses are not. (A) 'Narrowing to `bins/ctl/log/0/`, which drops the epoch, is NOT equivalent and is KILLED by 12 tests' -- measured FALSE for the narrowing the entry's own heading describes. `!key.startsWith(logPrefix.substring(0, logPrefix.length() - 17))`, which IS `bins/ctl/log/0/` for the LogKeys("bins",1) under test and is prefix-agnostic, leaves the whole suite GREEN (./gradlew :sequencer:test --rerun-tasks, BUILD SUCCESSFUL). (B) The 12 failures are reproducible only from a HARD-CODED literal, `!key.startsWith("bins/ctl/log/0/")`: exactly 12, which is where the number came from. They die because that literal names a `prefix` component most chains do not use -- CommitLogTest builds `new CommitLog(store, "p", 0)`, and LocalSequencerFailoverTest / LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest / LocalSequencerTest / CommitProtocolSimulation / InvariantFixtures all use PREFIX = "bins/cluster-a" -- so every real key of those chains is refused. (C) The stated mechanism, 'a sibling epoch's entries would be read into this chain', is false. I read all 12 failure messages out of the JUnit XML: every one is the refusal direction -- 'expected: 5L but was: 0L', 'expected: 8L but was: 0L', 'the epoch DOES see its own chain expected: 7L but was: 0L', two I2 violations and two 'seal did not converge'. Not one is cross-contamination, and it cannot be: both call sites ask about keys returned by `store.list(logPrefix, ...)` scoped to the FULL prefix, so a sibling epoch's key never reaches isEntryKey -- which is the same argument the entry itself makes three lines earlier. With only the operand narrowed, a sibling key also still fails the final `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))` and returns false. (D) Consequently 'THE BOUND IS THE EPOCH SEGMENT, NOT THE LENGTH' is wrong, and the first draft it says 'measurement refuted before it landed' was right: for every narrowing derived from logPrefix that I measured -- drop the trailing '/', drop the whole epoch segment -- the suite is green, and the kills start only at k <= prefix.length(), i.e. at the bare record component, which is exactly what the entry's LAST clause already names ('NOR IS startsWith(prefix) ... killed by test -- `bins.delta`'). The correction inverted a true statement on the strength of a measurement of a different mutant.
findings.failure_scenario: A session touching LogKeys after M4.8b2 -- say hoisting a shared `ctl/log/0/` constant when M4.8c's discovery lands, or reusing the guard for the checkpoint grammar -- reads baselines/mutants.txt to learn what constrains `isEntryKey`. It is told the epoch segment of the startsWith operand is pinned by 12 tests, so it does not add one. Nothing pins it: the derived narrowing is green across the whole sequencer suite, measured. The residue is the same unchecked-exception hazard this task exists to remove -- under any proper-prefix narrowing, `isEntryKey("bins/ctl/log/0/0000000000000001.delta")` slices substring(32,31) and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException where the predicate must answer false. That is the identical hazard the commit refused to argue for the two guard DELETIONS, and killed by test instead.
findings.remedy: Subtractive: delete the two ⚠️ clauses (the epoch bound and the 12-test claim). The entry's remaining text is true as measured. STRICTLY BETTER, and it deletes entry 3 outright: add one assertion to the existing LogKeysTest.aKeyTooSHORTToCarryTheGrammarIsRefusedRatherThanThrowing -- assertThat(KEYS.isEntryKey("bins/ctl/log/0/0000000000000001.delta")).isFalse() -- which I measured passing on the unmutated tree and killing EVERY proper-prefix narrowing: trailing-'/' drop, epoch drop, the hard-coded literal, and the bare `prefix` component (it subsumes the `bins.delta` case, which I verified by removing that case and watching the bare-prefix mutant still die). One line converts an argued survivor into a killed one.

findings.title: Arguing the startsWith narrowing is the wrong side of testing.md rule 9's 'killed or argued', and is inconsistent with the same commit's choice for the guard deletions
findings.detail: Rule 9 permits either, so this does not block on its own. But entries 1 and 2 are argued because they CANNOT be killed -- `contains(SUFFIX)` cannot change the return value and cannot throw while logPrefix holds no '.', and the reversed `equals` is a no-op since `key` is already dereferenced by the guards above -- whereas entry 3's mutant is not equivalent at all: it changes `false` into a thrown StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for `<any proper prefix of logPrefix>.delta`, and one measured assertion kills it. The commit already made the opposite call on the identical hazard: both guard DELETIONS are unreachable through today's two call sites for exactly the same reason entry 3 gives, and the backlog row records them as 'Killed rather than argued, because recovery dying on an unchecked exception is the exact failure this task exists to remove'. Same hazard, same reachability, opposite treatment, in one commit.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.8b2's writer asks isEntryKey about a key it is about to write rather than one it listed -- the exact call shape the backlog row anticipates. If the operand has drifted to any proper prefix of logPrefix by then, the writer gets an unchecked exception instead of a boolean, and no test in the tree fails.
findings.remedy: Same one-line assertion as T6's preferred remedy; then delete entry 3 from baselines/mutants.txt rather than correcting it.
